utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The Chamber was informed that the Prosecution would like to raise a preliminary matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. And may we move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. And the witness may be escorted into the courtroom. Meanwhile, I use the time to deal with a -- an item which is still on my agenda; it's about Prosecution expert witnesses. On the 22nd of December of last year, the Defence filed its Rule 94 bis notice and objection to the expert report submitted by the Prosecution as part of the reopening of its case. The Defence requested leave to exceed the word limit. Considering the number of experts dealt with in the filing, the Chamber hereby grants leave. The Prosecution responded on the 5th of January of this year. The Chamber understands that the Defence does not challenge the expertise of Ian Hanson and Tomas Parsons and that it does not object to their expert reports.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In light of this and having reviewed their CVs, the Chamber considers that they may testify as experts. The Defence wishes to cross-examine the two witnesses to clarify aspects of their reports or expertise. Since the Prosecution is planning to call these witnesses as part of the reopening of its case, they will be available for cross-examination by the Defence. In this respect, the Chamber notes that Parsons is to be recalled as he has given evidence previously. The Chamber defers its decision on admission into evidence of the reports for the witnesses until the time of their respective testimonies. The Chamber will deal with the Defence objections for the remaining four proposed expert witnesses in separate decisions. Good morning, Mr. Kalabic. Before we continue, I'd like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration that you have given yesterday at the beginning of your testimony, that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Mr. Traldi will now continue his cross-examination. Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, and good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can the Prosecution please have P7003 MFI, again.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, sir, I'm going to continue briefly looking at the 4th Session of the RS Assembly that we discussed yesterday. And as it comes up, just as a reminder, it's dated the 21st of December, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And if we could have page 43 in the English and 90 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And we see at the bottom of the page in the English and the middle of the page in the B/C/S, Professor Koljevic starts to speak.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning to page 44 in the English and 92 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Professor Koljevic refers first to a fundamental lie, that it is possible and desirable to live together. And then at the end of his remarks, he says: "Peace requires secure foundations. Peace can be built through continuing pacification and separation, and not through a false co-existence. That is precisely what we, as your representatives, have been advocating with the idea of a tripartite Bosnia and Herzegovina from the very start." Now, do you recall Professor Koljevic informing the Assembly that separation, and I'd put to you he meant separation among ethnic lines, was what the Bosnian Serb leadership had been advocating from the start?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember Koljevic's speech. It was a really long time ago in the distant past. I really can't remember what he was saying. I don't remember what he said at that session.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Is it your evidence that you do or don't recall that the Bosnian Serb leadership did, in fact, take the position that there should be a separation of the peoples of Bosnia and Herzegovina along ethnic lines.

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that happening at that session.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you remember it happening at any point?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Traldi, because we are -- I get a bit confused. Your previous -- your first question was about - specifically - about what Professor Koljevic said informing the Assembly, and we are now slowly -- we should clearly distinguish between with what was said at that time and what -- whether what was said is in accordance with the policy pursued at the time by the leadership.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I take your point, Mr. President. And I'll do it in a few steps, if you don't mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: First, sir, do you recall at any point the Bosnian Serb leadership taking the position that the peoples of Bosnia and Herzegovina should be separated along ethnic lines?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am trying to recall. I believe that such a position did surface at one point. When all the negotiations fell through with regard to the -- to Bosnia remain in Yugoslavia, the leadership did indeed take such a position with regard to secession, e.g., how shall I put it, the regionalisation of Bosnia and Herzegovina or the division of Bosnia into canton. Each of the cantons would have a majority people. Each of the peoples would have a part of Bosnia and Herzegovina to itself, that is. I believe that it was very much along the lines of Cutileiro's plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So you recall this happening, you say, when the negotiations fell through. Would it refresh your recollection if I suggested to you that you were describing events in late March 1992?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you have in mind. What is it that I should try and remember?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: When you say the negotiations fell through with regard to Bosnia remaining in Yugoslavia and you refer to Cutileiro, I'd put to you you're describing late March 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serbs thought that Yugoslavia would continue. They thought so in March, April, May, and June, so I really wouldn't be able to pin-point a time the way you suggest I should.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, I'll explore your evidence in that respect perhaps a little bit more later. Before I move on from this question, though, the Trial Chamber has received evidence that not just Mr. Koljevic on this occasion but repeatedly at Bosnian Serb assembly sessions as early as 1991, like in this instance, members of the Bosnian Serb leadership discussed the separation of the peoples of Bosnia along ethnic lines. Is it really your evidence that you don't remember that ever coming up?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The way individual discussions on that topic, but I don't remember that such a decision was ever reached [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have P3771. And, Your Honour, for this one we'll simply ensure that the document is still MFI'd, but all of these remarks are part of the eventual excerpt that we seek to have admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, sir, as P3771 comes up, these are the minutes -- or these will be the minutes of the 6th Meeting of the Executive Committee of the SDS Municipal Board in Kljuc held two days later, the 23rd of December.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And if we could have page 2 in both the English and B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I'm going to direct your attention to the very end of point 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And perhaps we could rotate the B/C/S just for ease of use.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just to the very end of point 1, we see your name twice. The first time it reads: "After a recess, Rajko Kalabic informed those present on the issues considered in the second part of the Serbian Assembly proceedings." Now, first, those assembly proceedings, that refers to the assembly two days earlier that we just looked at; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not understand your question at all, and I was listening very carefully.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This document reflects that on the 23rd of December, 1991 you informed the Kljuc SDS about the issues considered in the second part of the Serbian assembly proceedings, so I'd put to you that refers to the session of the assembly held two days earlier. Yesterday you suggested that you didn't think you had informed the Kljuc SDS about what happened at that assembly session, and so I'd ask if these minutes refresh your recollection as to whether you, in fact, did so.

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't jog my memory at all. As I'm looking at this part of the minutes that is in front of me, where it says "Rajko Kalabic informed all the present ..." and so on and so forth, from this part of the minutes, I don't see what was it that I informed the attendants about at that session. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking you a very simple question for the moment. It says that you informed them about what was discussed at the Serbian assembly. That's the Serbian assembly held two days earlier, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand whether that was the session that was dealt with in the previous question. Is that the same session?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The previous questions have referred to the session that was held two days earlier. I'd put to you that's the session being referred to here. Do you agree or disagree? And I'd appreciate a "yes" or "no" answer.

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't remember. I can't remember what it was that I informed the gathered people about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, let me stop you there. That's about content. When you informed those present at the local SDS meeting in Kljuc about the Serbian assembly proceedings, was that the assembly that took place two days before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Probably, but I can't remember any detail.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, we didn't ask you to remember any further details. Would there be any other assembly session that you would report about on the 23rd of January other than the 21st of January assembly meeting -- I should -- I missed -- I should have said "December." Could you think of any other assembly meeting that you would report about on the 23rd of December?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember whether any other assembly meeting was held.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could have page 1 of this document in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I'm going to see if I have any better luck refreshing your recollection as to what Veljko Kondic reported about. Here at the top of item 1, it says: "Veljko Kondic informed the meeting of the instructions for the organisation and activities of the Serbian people in BH." And that: "All organs will be required to act in accordance with the instructions." Now, that refers to the Variant A and B document we saw yesterday; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so. However, I can't tell that from the minutes. But I suppose that you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, in fact, you recall that Veljko Kondic spoke specifically about Variant A; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Veljko Kondic briefly explained Variant A.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And below that, we see Brane Vojvodic say: "I can accept all Karadzic's proposals without seeing them." And Kondic replies: "That means that all suggestions and tasks from the instructions are accepted in their entirety." So the suggestions and tasks from the Variant A and B instructions were accepted in their entirety by the Kljuc SDS; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to see that part of the document that the Prosecutor is talking about. It must be on the second page and I only have the first page of the document, so I'm not in a position to see and to follow what the Prosecutor is saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think if we scroll maybe to the very top of the second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The last name I see here is Jovanka Cvijic, and I see that's two lines above what we are discussing in the ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The words spoken by Brane Vojvodic was, I suppose, on the last line of the previous page.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Is that not -- do you see now the text we were looking at or the text we were discussing?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that part of the text. Brane Vojvodic shared his opinion and no vote was taken. Staff members were just briefed and they were not asked to vote either for or against.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: But as I put to you, the instructions were, in fact, accepted in their entirety, right, by the Kljuc SDS? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Kljuc SDS did not consider the instructions in their entirety. Only Variant A was presented to its members. Nobody informed anybody about Variant B because that variant, Variant B, did not refer to Kljuc at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I appreciate your precision but I think you're still not quite answering the question. Was Variant A accepted and implemented in Kljuc by the Municipal Board at this time? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: In it's entirety.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In it's entirety, as reflected by Mr. Kondic's statement.

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Variant A referred to those municipalities where the SDS is --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- was in power --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and in Kljuc --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not asking you which municipalities were referred to by which variant. What I'm asking you is, as Veljko Kondic says here, Variant A and suggestions and tasks included in it were accepted in their entirety by the Kljuc SDS at this time. That's correct, isn't it? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer just with a yes or a no because it does not reflect the true picture of what had been happening. If you allow me, I would like to explain briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'd be very grateful, sir, if, before explaining, you gave an answer as to whether the Kljuc SDS accepted Variant A of the instructions at this time.

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Variant A, the SDS had no need to accept that, because this variant explained the performance of power over there where it already existed. So it was just copied, the method of exercising power in those municipalities where somebody was already in power, so nothing was invented there. And then, according to that variant, work would continue. Variant B --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Okay. Sir --

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- was not the subject of --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- you've, again, you're describing the mechanics of the variants, and while it's interesting, it's not what I'd asked you about. As to the implementation of Variant A, just for instance, we see below Mr. Kondic's statement that all suggestions and tasks are accepted in their entirety, that a Crisis Staff is formed. That's one of the tasks set out in Variant A of the instructions; right? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We see a few lines below it that someone is appointed to be responsible for co-operation with the SDA. Variant A of the instructions also says somebody should be appointed to do that; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So when you say the SDS had no need to accept that a few lines earlier, in fact what happened, as we see on this page, immediately after the text to which I had directed your attention, the SDS implementing instructions contained in Variant A. That's the truth, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the SDS co-operated with the SDA even before this meeting. Immediately after the elections and throughout, they co-operated with the SDA. So that is something that was already underway. It was just being confirmed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, please focus on the questions. The instructions were to appoint someone, that's what happens, and no one suggested - not Mr. Traldi, not anyone else - that there had been no co-operation whatsoever. Mr. Traldi focuses on the implementation of, in this example, just this instruction. Would you please stick to the question rather than to repeatedly give context which, apparently, you consider more relevant. It's Mr. Traldi who asks the questions. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm done with this document. Could we have 65 ter 31814, page 73.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, sir, just before closing the topic of Variant A and B, we discussed yesterday the dissemination of those instructions through SDS representatives, and in that context I want to look at one part of your testimony in the Brdjanin case, which is now on our screens on the left. Now, you were asked: "You told us that you got," and this is beginning at line 22 here, "you saw a copy of the instructions for the organisation of the Serbian people in Sarajevo?" You responded: "Yes, I did say that I saw this instruction in Sarajevo." And you were asked: "It was given, was it not, to representatives in the assembly to ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And then we'll turn the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: "... to take back to their own municipalities?" And you said: "No, it wasn't given to representatives in the assembly. It was given to representatives of the Serbian Democratic Party, and they were the ones who brought these instructions to their respective municipalities." Do you stand behind this portion of your testimony in the Brdjanin case as truthful and accurate?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: All right. Now, a few days after the meeting we just looked at, Kljuc municipality joined the Autonomous Region of Krajina; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A few days after that, the municipality of Kljuc carried out a change of name of the region. Beforehand, it was called the Community of Municipalities of Banja Luka, and at that moment when this was done, this community --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- got the name of the Autonomous Region of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'd suggest to you that, in fact, that name change took place in September of 1991. What I'm putting to you is that in late December 1991, three days after the meeting we just looked at on the 23rd of December, Kljuc decided to accede or decided on its accession to the autonomous region. That's true, right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 02996.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is a decision by the Kljuc Municipal Assembly, dated the 16th of January, 1992, signed by Jovo Banjac. Directing your attention to the end of the preamble, we read: "The Kljuc Municipal Assembly, at its 10th Session held on 26th December, 1991, adopted the following decision on the accession of Kljuc municipality to the Autonomous Region of Bosnian Krajina." So, in fact, on the 26th of December, 1991 Kljuc did decide on its accession to the Bosnian Krajina, to the ARK; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is an explanation in paragraph number 1. It says here that: "The earlier adopted decision on the accession of Kljuc municipality to the Banja Luka Community of Municipalities is hereby confirmed and a decision adopted for Kljuc municipality to accede to the Regional Community of Bosnian Krajina, now the Autonomous Region of Bosnian Krajina."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We have just finished the paragraph and we have not interpreted what the witness said very fast after that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat what you said after you had read paragraph 1 of this decision, because you were speaking so speedily that the interpreters could not follow you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So this is what paragraph 1 says: "The earlier adopted decision on the accession of Kljuc municipality to the Banja Luka Community of Municipalities is hereby confirmed and a decision adopted for Kljuc municipality to ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. What did you add? Last time when you read this you added some comment or whatever. What did you then say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that that Community of Municipalities of Banja Luka from that time would be called the Autonomous Region of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's move on. The text seems to be that there was an earlier decision which was confirmed and that now a new decision was adopted. Let's -- unless there is any specific issue about it, Mr. Traldi, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I will, Your Honours. I'd just tender the document before doing so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 2996 receives number P7030, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, sir, in February 1992 an engineering unit of the JNA was transferred from Knin to Kljuc municipality; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That unit was transferred to the municipality of Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And it was located in a commercial facility owned by Sipad Kljuc; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was not in Kljuc. Sipad is a complex company; inter alia, it included forestry. Forestry Sumarsva had a unit of their own in a forest in the direction of Bosanski Petrovac. That work organisation was far away from the seat of the municipality of Kljuc. It was 20 kilometres away, and that's where this engineering unit was located.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That was in the area of Laniste in the municipality of Kljuc; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was in the area of Laniste. Laniste belonged to the municipality of Kljuc, and it was at the border with the municipality of Petrovac; Bosanski Petrovac, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And in May 1992 when the transformation of the military took place, that unit became part of the VRS; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Staying with February 1992, you attended a meeting in Sarajevo in February 1992 and you stayed at the Holiday Inn; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember. I mean, staying at the Holiday Inn. I think -- I mean, I did stay there once. Once. I don't know what month that was when I stayed at the Holiday Inn hotel. Every other time I went to Sarajevo, I stayed at a private apartment in Ciglane, which is a part of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 07102, page 6 in the English and page 8 in the B/C/S. I know we don't have the right page on the screen yet. It's page 6 in the English and 8 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, we see R. Kalabic at the top. We see arrival, the 14th of February; departure, the 15th of February. Does that refresh your recollection as to the occasion that you stayed at the Holiday Inn while you were in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot see the guest's signature here. If I stayed at this hotel, I would have signed this bill, but I don't see my signature here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And if -- if an organisation had been paying the bills for a number of people who stayed there together, you wouldn't necessarily have had to sign yourself, would you?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. But this organisation just provided, I mean, a list of people who were supposed to come. They did not check who it was that had come and who had not come. How the payments were made, I really cannot say.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And -- I -- we both used the word "organisation" but we're talking about the SDS; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The SDS provided a list of persons who were supposed to attend the meeting. Now, whether each and every one of these persons did attend and did spend the night there, I don't know. One cannot see that on the basis of this bill.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Okay. Let's set aside what you can see on the basis of this bill. Do you recall whether you yourself attended a meeting in the Holiday Inn on the 14th and 15th of February, 1992?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really cannot remember whether I was there or not. I've been trying, but I cannot.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: All right. I'll just put to you briefly: The Chamber has received evidence that, among other things, Radovan Karadzic activated the second level of the Variant A and B instructions at that meeting --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- and it's the Prosecution's position that you then briefed the Kljuc SDS about what had happened at the meeting. Do you recall either of those things having happened?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall. But if there is a document, I would like to have it on the screen so that it could jog my memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I am going to move on, but I'd ask that this be marked for identification and we'll make a selection from the receipts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could you assign a number for this series of documents.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 7102 receives number P7031, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is marked for identification. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, can the Prosecution please have 65 ter 03011.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, sir, as it comes up, these will be the minutes from the 8th Session of the Kljuc Municipal Board dated the 29th of April, 1992. So we're moving forward in time. By this point, the end of April, Serbs controlled the important positions in Kljuc and the power in Kljuc was really in Serb hands; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the Serbs had under their control, but they did share power with the SDA as we have stated previously; in the statement, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Okay. We see at point 2, current issues. Number 1, Veljko Kondic speaks. And below that, Vinko Kondic speaks. And Vinko Kondic says in the middle of the paragraph --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I'm told we should turn to the next page in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And Vinko Kondic, in the middle of the paragraph of his remarks --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sorry, if I could have just one moment. Okay. I'm told it's at the top of the page in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And in the middle of the paragraph, he says: "Serbs are the majority population in Kljuc. We control all the important positions." Now that is, in fact, the truth as of the 29th of April, 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't agree with his statement, and I cannot find that here on the top of this page, and I cannot read it myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was read to you literally, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning to page 2 in the English now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Veljko Kondic this time is speaking, and he says: "I take as my starting point the situation in Kljuc as it really is. The power in Kljuc is really in the hands of Serbs." That, too, is the truth of the situation as of 29 April 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is his statement, but I cannot confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 3011 receives number P7032, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, a few days after this, in fact, the Bosnian Serb authorities in Kljuc did take over power on the 7th of May; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no, they did not take over power. They had no one to take it from because they themselves were in power together with the SDA. It was the Serbs and the Muslims who were in power, and it's not that they had to take power over from someone else. If they had taken over power from the Muslims, then I would say that, yes, that would be the case, but no, that was not true. They were both in power as stated in the statement, and the statement has been admitted. On the 7th of May on the municipality building, the Yugoslav flag was replaced with a flag of Republika Srpska. That was done. And from that moment onwards, this question has been raised, power has been taken over. So in Bosnia-Herzegovina, everybody placed their own flags and insignia wherever they lived and worked. That was the case throughout Bosnia-Herzegovina, not only Kljuc. Kljuc was the last place where the flag of Yugoslavia was taken down from the municipality building and where the flag of Republika Srpska was put up.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: One of the other things that happened on that day was the police insignia was changed, right, to the new Republika Srpska police insignia?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both police and military insignia were changed. The five-pointed red star --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- that was worn until then --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- was replaced --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- I'm sorry to interrupt. But I'm not asking you to describe the JNA insignia. I'm asking you on the 7th of May the insignia on police uniforms in Kljuc was changed to the new Republika Srpska police insignia; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Asked and answered, line 22.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right. They were changed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: By the way, my microphone did not activate as I pushed it. The question was asked, the question was answered. You stopped the witness when he'd started explaining things you did not ask. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Fair enough, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As to the police in Kljuc, the Kljuc police was subordinated to the CSB in Banja Luka; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. That's the way it was according to hierarchy.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now before the conflict began, the highest-ranking Muslim police officer in Kljuc was the SJB commander Atif Dzafic; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you were asked yesterday about some Muslims and Croats who -- a small number who you said stayed in their jobs. What happened to Mr. Dzafic was that he was arrested a few weeks after this, taken to the Sanica school gym, then the Nikola Mackic school, and then the Sitnica school, and then he and a large number of other people were made to walk -- other Muslims to walk from Sitnica to Manjaca camp. Were you also aware of that?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I am about to turn to a new topic. I know we're a minute or two early but I'd suggest it's a good time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll take the break now. Witness, we would like to see you back in 20 minutes. You may now follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at 10 minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If I could just raise one very quick matter. I know we have a number of housekeeping matters pending which we will attend to given opportunities over the next few days, but with respect to one that was on the list regarding P6889, a document that was MFI'd, the Defence and the Prosecution will be in discussion about that. So I just wanted to alert the Court to the fact that there may be further developments so that the Court didn't unilaterally undertake any action on that before we concluded our efforts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll check whether it's somewhere on our list already. Perhaps P6689 -- yup, P6889. Mr. Traldi, if you're ready, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Can we have 65 ter 31850. And I think we only need one version, so we could zoom in a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, sir, we're looking here at an aerial image of Kljuc town taken after the war. Do you see the municipality building on this image?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to ask that the usher assist you in making several markings, and I'm going to ask that you wait for me to instruct you what to mark and then we'll go one by one. Can you first circle the municipality building.

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And that was where the Crisis Staff had its meetings; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could you -- Krizni Stab inside that circle to identify the building.

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Okay. Do you see the Nikola Mackic school on this image?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could you circle that as well, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours, we're being told we'll need a moment for the court reporter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then we'll just take our time. I noticed ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, I saw that the witness marked the school already but the question for him to mark the school is not on the record yet. Could you please repeat that question and then we take it that what the witness marked is the school but perhaps you'll ask him to add some letters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The previous one --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- about KS is not recorded properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, sir, just solely to complete the transcript --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, both.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: To complete the transcript, you've written a KS on the building that you circled for Krizni Stab, that's the municipality building, and you've circled another building, which is the Nikola Mackic school; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can I ask you to write simply an S for school inside the circle on the Nikola Mackic school.

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And do you see the Kljuc SJB building? The building that has the Kljuc SJB in 1992 on this image.

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I appreciate you waiting. Could you circle that as well, please.

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And can you mark an SJB there.

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, we see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: For my clarity, is it the brown building or is it the green building? The brown building [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Green building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, do you see on this image where the 17th Brigade of the VRS was headquartered once it was created?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of the fact that the 17th Brigade was deployed in the city located there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Then I won't ask you to mark anything for that. One more question on this image. We see a mosque just below the SJB building. That was built only after the war; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd tender this image as marked by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31850, as marked by the witness, receives number P7033, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, sir, I'm going to turn to two meetings you attended a few days after the take-over of Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have P2867.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, if you want to consult with counsel, take off your earphones and speak at such a volume that it's inaudible for other persons in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, these are the minutes of a meeting held by the Command of the 1st Partizan Brigade with presidents of municipalities in the zone of responsibility of the division, and it's dated the 14th of May, 1992. We see here at number 11, below Colonel Galic, Colonel Basara, and others that you attended this meeting; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And this meeting was held in Kljuc; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 3 in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We see the president of Mrkonjic Grad, Mr. Malidza, presented conclusions from the meeting held in Banja Luka, and it refers to renaming of the army. And then below that, it reads: "The strategic goals formulated at the meeting in Banja Luka were presented," and it refers to six, the first of which is state separation of the three national communities. Now, you know these to be consistent with the six strategic objectives formulated at the 16th Assembly in Banja Luka two days earlier; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware of the fact that that was defined in Banja Luka, but the bullet points 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 were defined as it is presented in here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And those were the strategic objectives of the Serb people; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And they had been first articulated, it says, at the meeting in Banja Luka here. That refers to the 16th Assembly, the 16th Session of the Bosnian Serb Assembly; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember which assembly meeting it was, but that was what happened at an assembly meeting. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And what we see here, I won't insist on the number, but what we see here is the local military and political authorities meeting and, among other things, discussing the implementation of the decisions and goals reached at the republic level; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that meeting, people were informed about the objectives. I don't know who said what and how much people spoke, at what length. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We saw only 11 names listed at the beginning. Do you recall about how many people attended this meeting?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: All right. Let's move on then to P3747. Now, these are meetings -- these are minutes, rather, of a meeting of the Kljuc Crisis Staff held on the 13th and 14th of May, 1992, and we see at the top that you were absent on the 13th. I want to direct your attention to a couple of specific points.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: First, if we could have page 2 in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We see item 2, and it says you and Jovo Banjac advised the members of the Crisis Staff of the positions on the security situation in Kljuc municipality in connection with the decisions and reports from a session of the Serbian Republic of BH Assembly. Now, you passed on to the Kljuc Crisis Staff, among other things, the strategic objectives that you'd heard discussed at the meeting we just looked at; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that I attended that meeting at all in the first place, because on the 14th, which is -- what it says here, that I was there, I believe that I was at another meeting. There is a document to that effect. Maybe you should look for it and you would see that the two meetings coincided. I couldn't be in two places at the same time. I really can't remember that I took the floor at this particular meeting because, according to me, I never attended it in the first place.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would only ask if counsel is going to ask about the meeting that we just looked at, that they specify. Because the questions in relation to the prior document talked about two meetings. So by not differentiating between the two, we'd have an unclear record as to which one the witness is being asked about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that we had a meeting with the persons from the various municipalities where Mr. Galic was present, that was one meeting; and then the other one is the assembly meeting which was -- took place in two days, the 13th and the 14th. If I understand well --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It might be best if I re-ask the question and clearly distinguish -- and I'm happy to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So, sir, what we just saw is these strategic objectives I had put to you were set out on the 12th. On the 14th, we just saw you attended a meeting with Colonel Galic and others, and at that meeting the strategic objectives were discussed with leaders from a variety of different municipalities, and what I am putting to you is that at this meeting you and Mr. Banjac also relayed the strategic objectives to the Kljuc Crisis Staff, this meeting on the 14th also held in Kljuc. That's the truth, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that this is not the truth. I simply did not attend that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The records -- well, let me ask a couple of follow-up questions. You attended Crisis Staff meetings regularly; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here that I was absent from the Crisis Staff meeting on the 13th, which means that I did not attend those meetings regularly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, being absent at one moment doesn't say anything about regular attending meetings, Witness, so could you please refrain from conclusions and rather stick to facts. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, what I'm putting to you is, and I'll do it in a quick and simple way, everybody at the Crisis Staff knew who you were. Relaying conclusions from the assembly was part of your job as an assembly member. These minutes are accurate and you are, at the moment, trying to minimise your involvement in the dissemination of these strategic objectives from the Bosnian Serb leadership to the Bosnian Serb leadership in Kljuc. Do you have any comment on that?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: All right. Then I'm going to turn to May 27th.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I'm done with this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In paragraph 17 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I still would have a question for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You earlier you have seen minutes of a meeting which took place on the 13th and 14th of May; that's how it is reported. It specifically says that you were not present on the 13th, which again suggests that you were present at the 14th because otherwise it would have said that you were not present on the 13th and the 14th. Now you, in one of your answers, you suggested that you would not have attended the meeting, and I'm now focusing on the 14th of May, because you remember that you had another meeting. Could you tell us what that other meeting would have been?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't remember the meeting and what meeting it was, but I know that there was certainly a meeting on the 14th and I know that I attended it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now we have looked at another meeting on the 14th; that was the meeting with the leaders of the municipalities together with General Galic. Did you refer to that meeting or did you refer to another meeting?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I might assist. That's P2867 is the document --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the meeting you're referring to. Yes. Now we just had a look at the minutes of that meeting which indicates --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's the meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, the minutes of that meeting says that it was, I think, finished at 3.00 in the afternoon or at least shortly after lunchtime and that the other meeting started at 6.00. We looked at the minutes of those as well. So I'm just putting to you, and whether you have any comment, that a meeting in the early afternoon would not prevent you from being present later that day in a meeting on that same 14th of April with the Crisis Staff of the Kljuc municipality. And I'm asking you for comment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If meetings were held at different times, and if I attended that particular meeting, then my task would have been to brief the Crisis Staff on the positions of the Assembly of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I really can't remember whether I attended that meeting or not but this is how things would have happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I am going to turn now to the end of May. In paragraph 17 of your statement, you mention that a VRS unit arrived in Kljuc on the 27th of May from the Kula barracks and that the unit was under the command of then-Colonel Galic. And that was a unit of the 30th Partizan Division of the VRS; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, prior to the 27th of May, for several days the Kljuc Secretariat for National Defence had been mobilising people into the 30th Division; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the decision of mobilisation that the Kljuc Secretariat for National Defence was implementing had been reached by the leadership of the Republika Srpska; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mobilisation did take place based on the decisions made by the competent authority of Republika Srpska, from the top leadership of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Okay. Once this VRS unit got into Kljuc, it set up checkpoints on the roads into Kljuc; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After the 27th of May, check-points were established at certain places around Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Colonel Galic personally remained in Kljuc for the next several days; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw Colonel Galic only in the office of the president of the municipality. As for where he was when he was not in that office, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, you said he came on the 27th. You've said you were also in a meeting with him on June 1st. Do you know him to have left Kljuc in the interim?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He left the office of the president of the municipality. That I know. But I certainly don't know whether he left Kljuc because I wasn't following him around.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, he and other VRS officers attended meetings that the Crisis Staff held during this period of several days; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, on the 27th and for another day or two Colonel Galic was present. As for other meetings, I can't recall, I mean, who was present after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: All right. I want to look now at some of the -- at some more of the specific actions that he and his unit took. In paragraph 18 of your statement, you mentioned that after the attacks on Serb police and soldiers in Kljuc on the 27th of May, weapons were collected in Pudin Han, Velagici, Krasulje, Biljani, Sanica, and Kamicak. These weapons were collected by Colonel Galic's VRS unit; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was the army that collected them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And that unit also during this time shelled Pudin Han, inter alia, destroying the mosque there; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At one moment, yes. Pudin Han was shelled. But who it was that destroyed the mosque, I really have no information about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: While Colonel Galic was in Kljuc, he informed the Crisis Staff that he was ordering the creation of a town defence command, and he appointed a local reserve officer, Marko Adamovic, as its commander; radio it?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I may just interrupt. Sir, you've just said you don't know who destroyed the mosque. Do you know who shelled Pudin Han?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Army of Republika Srpska shelled it. It was mortars of a smaller calibre. Just a few of these shells, I mean.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we please have P3758.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we're waiting for that, could the witness explain to us how he knew that it was just a few shells and what their approximate number was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Three or four shells. The firing of shells could be heard in Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you say three or four shells were fired at Kljuc. Could -- were shells fired at Pudin Han and you could hear that from Kljuc, and that's the basis for your observation. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, before I go through this document, just to be fair to you, I'm going to put to you that, in fact, there was -- it's the Prosecution's position that, in fact, there was massive shelling of Pudin Han and large-scale destruction inflicted. Now, you couldn't see the village yourself, could you?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The shelling was really the way I said. As for more significant destruction, that happened later when weapons were being taken from people who were organised in a paramilitary territorial defence, the Muslim paramilitary territorial defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So you're suggesting that the destruction of Pudin Han occurred during a disarmament operation and not during the shelling that preceded it, just so I understand your evidence; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Pudin Han was not destroyed. It was not destroyed. After an intervention by Republika Srpska, some houses were set on fire and that was it at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: All right. This is -- now, this is the book of minutes from sessions of the Kljuc Municipal Assembly Crisis Staff --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I'll leave that topic for the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the purpose of a book like this is to record and memorialise the discussions and the conclusions at Crisis Staff sessions; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time I see this book and that I see it written this way. I assume that this is a compilation of minutes from sessions of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the purpose of the minutes is, as I stated, to record and memorialise the discussions and conclusions at the Crisis Staff sessions; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, minutes were kept at each and every meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I don't think you've quite answered my question, and I'm afraid I'm going to insist. The purpose of the minutes is to record and memorialise the discussions and the conclusions that occur at those meetings; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether that's the case, but I know that minutes were kept at each and every session.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 5 in the English and page 8 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We're seeing here the minutes on the 29th of May, 1992, and it's recorded that the Crisis Staff is in continuous session and is following events in the area of the municipality since combat operations are ongoing and reports from the field are arriving constantly. I'm going to ask you several very specific questions about these minutes. First, was it Colonel Galic personally or was it one of his subordinates who would inform the Crisis Staff about events in the field?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly it was Colonel Galic who came during those few days to Crisis Staff sessions, and he would provide brief information about what had happened in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, one of his subordinates, a brigade commander named Lieutenant-Colonel Vukasevic, would also attend meetings during this period, right, at times?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Vukasevic is someone I saw only once, and had you not mentioned him, I don't think I would have remembered his name anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'll ask you a little bit about him shortly. But turning --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sorry. Turning to page 6 in the English and 10 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We see at point 1 a decision of the commander to block several villages with the obligation of calling for unconditional surrender and surrender of arms. And then if no resistance is given, the mopping up of the area can be carried out. The commander being referred to is again Colonel Galic; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am trying to find his name here but I cannot, and I cannot remember whether those were his words.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, when you read the commander has taken the decision to block those villages, who do you understand to have been the commander?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in the military hierarchy I cannot know, and I did not know then, who the commander was on the ground, whether it was Colonel Galic or whether it was the mentioned Vukasevic or a third person. I really cannot recall right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I want to turn now, then, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just to close that topic, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So, you understand that decision to have been taken by one of the VRS commanders and you don't recall which one; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I want to turn now then to the meeting you described yesterday held a couple of days later where you and Colonel Galic learned that Muslims detained at the Velagici school had been massacred. Now, the military command in the area had assigned people to guard those prisoners; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the case that that evening the military command placed guards to guard the people who were detained in the facility and to guard the facility itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Okay. And at this meeting when you heard about the massacre, you mentioned that you, Colonel Galic, and Jovo Banjac were present. I'm just going to ask you if a few other people were present at the time. Was Bosko Lukic present?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember who was present, who all the people present were, but the three was that I mentioned, I'm sure. There were other persons there, but who it was exactly I cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So you specifically don't recall if Bosko Lukic was there; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you three more names and simply say "yes, I recall that he was there," or "no, I recall he wasn't there," or "I don't recall," please. First, Vinko Kondic, do you recall if he was there?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From time to time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: At this specific meeting.

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that he was there on the 30th of May. I really don't remember whether he was at the meeting on the 30th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And just to be perfectly clear, we're talking about the meeting where you learned --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And maybe for clarity, let's take the document off the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The meeting where you learned about the massacre at Velagici. Do you recall if Vinko Kondic was there when you learned that?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the 27th of May, and Vinko Kondic was present at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It's -- it's the 1st of June that the massacre happened; right? The massacre at Velagici of the detained Muslims.

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember whether Vinko Kondic was at the meeting on the 1st of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you recall if Lieutenant-Colonel Vukasevic, who we discussed a moment ago, was there when you learned that the Muslim had been massacred?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Galic was the only officer present there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And do you recall if Ljuban Bajic from the SDS was there?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He probably was, but I really cannot recall. I cannot say "yes" or "no." Perhaps I can remember as I look at the minutes. I see that Veljko Kondic wrote the minutes, so he was the fourth person that I know attended the meeting for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you claimed yesterday that the perpetrators of this massacre were tried. I'd put to you that they were arrested and taken to military prison and gave statements but, in fact, they were not put on trial or punished during the war. That's the truth, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I don't know. I know that they were arrested and tried, and how far that went I really don't know because I was not in a position to find anything out.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, that's the second time that you've testified that they were tried. What I'm putting to you is you, in fact, don't know whether there was a trial or not; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether there was a trial, but I know that they were arrested and that a process had started. But how far it went and whether it was completed, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So you don't know that they were released shortly thereafter?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I rise as I've consulted with my colleague, Mr. Lukic, just to make sure I wasn't missing something, but the B/C/S answers that I've been hearing over the earpiece of the witness have been talking about the B/C/S word "procesuiran", procesuiran," which is different from "tried," so I think there is a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's seek -- let's try to clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- might just have done so. He agreed that he doesn't know there was a trial and that there was a process. So I think that by this point we may have reached --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But that still suggests that the language he's using in one way or another -- let me try to clarify this. Witness, we understand a trial to be that an accused is brought before a court which will then determine whether the accused is guilty of the charges and if so to be punished. Did we understand well that you do not know whether those who were arrested for the events in the Nonide [phoen] Velagici school ever appeared before the judge in order to final determine whether or not they are guilty of the crimes charged?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know whether they appeared before a judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could have P3758 back. And turn to page 9 in the English and 15 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, here we're looking at the minutes from the Crisis Staff session on the 2nd of June, and we see at point 1(a), a report from the brigade commander, Lieutenant-Colonel and it's spelled Vucovecic, that is, in fact, Lieutenant-Colonel Vukasevic who we've been discussing; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it is Vukasevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now can the Prosecution please have P3528, page 12 in the English and page 9 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, sir, as this comes up, this will be a portion of the Velagici case file.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, document is under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- could you consider -- I do not know what questions you want to put to the witness, but to consider whether or not to go into private session if the document is under seal?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, actually, I'll just put to you the evidence the Chamber has received. My notes appear to be inconsistent on this point. But the Chamber has received evidence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: At least it should not be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And it certainly should not be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And it -- the Chamber has received evidence that shortly before giving this report, Lieutenant-Colonel Vukasevic had been at the Velagici school and had ordered the engineering unit to organise a truck and a bulldozer to transport the bodies from Velagici to the woods on the road to Gornji Budelj village. Now, I have three questions for you on this point. First, did he mention issuing this order when he was giving a report to the Crisis Staff the next day?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that something like that was mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Second, the engineering unit, that would have been the engineering unit based at Laniste that we discussed earlier this morning; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume that that is the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And third, are you aware that the bodies of the people killed in this massacre were exhumed after the war from a pit in the Laniste area in the woods off the road headed west from Velagici?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that there was an exhumation, but I really don't know where or when that exactly took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now shortly after these meetings, the Velagici school was blown up; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the old abandoned school from the old days, and I really don't know. I'm not sure about it being blown up. I haven't heard about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Did you ever pass in that direction during the war?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did pass, but the school is away from the road and there are other buildings there and the terrain is such that the school cannot actually be seen. At least that's the way I remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, could we have P4157, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is an aerial image of Velagici area, and we can see on the left an image as of the 13th of November, 1990 and on the right as of the 21st of August, 1992. I admit the quality isn't perfect, but if you look at the area within the dotted lines on both sides you can make out the outlines of buildings on the left, can't you, within those dotted lines?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I assume that the black areas are buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And not on the right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume that the black are buildings, but the image is really such that I cannot give a relevant answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Fair enough. Now as of -- as of the date of this massacre, the 1st of June, the fighting in Kljuc had been finished with; right? Fighting in Kljuc municipality.

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the town of Kljuc there wasn't any fighting. There was fighting only in those areas where the Territorial Defence had been organised, the Muslim Territorial Defence. In those parts. I've already said in my statement where the fighting had taken place.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, those -- those areas, Pudin Han and others, the fighting there was over by the 1st of June, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot recall right now when all of that was over.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, could we have 65 ter 030 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we do so, Mr. Traldi. Could I ask you one follow-up question. You said you couldn't see the school because it was away from the road. The area indicated here, is that the area where the school was located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, that's what I assume, although I cannot state anything with certainty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So are you sure that the location of the school was away from the road and, if so, at what distance approximately?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that part, the road was deeply cut in, so that cannot be noticed if one goes there by car because it's very steep and one cannot see on either side of the road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know whether the Prosecution has any pictures or images of it so as to better be able to verify the accuracy of the witness here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I admit I'm not sure off the top of my head, but we'll certainly look, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please do so and then perhaps share that with the Defence and inform the Chamber if it sheds any light on the credibility or reliability of the witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, what's now at the site where the school was is a cemetery; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the cemetery is across the road from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And of course clearly visible from the road; right? As the road exists today anyway.

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the appearance of the road, but if you are headed from Kljuc to Bihac, the cemetery is on the right-hand side of the road, and the neighbourhood where the school was located was on the left-hand side of the road. That's the way I remembered it, but I don't know. I can't -- I can't believe that I'm -- would have made such a mistake of not locating those two things properly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, Witness, could I ask you the following. You said: "I don't remember the appearance of the road." A minute ago you told us that the road was so deep that you couldn't overlook what was next to the road. Are you certain about that? Because you now say you don't remember the appearance of the road.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The second question about the appearance of the road. It's not that I did not realise what the appearance of the road was then. I don't know what its appearance is today. I don't know whether there were any new constructions. But the last time I passed that way, I know and I saw that the cemetery is on the right-hand side, that the school was on the left-hand side, and I know that the road is kind of -- that it curves next to the school and not next to the cemetery. The cemetery is a bit further away from the school. It's not just opposite the school across the road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You said --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- the Prosecution's question says: "As the road exists today anyway," at lines 21, 24 through 25.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm aware of that. You said the last time you passed that way. When was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Last year, sometime in the summer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you said that when you passed there last time, the cemetery is on the right-hand side. Could you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The school was on the left-hand side. Could you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are lots of buildings there nowadays, so it was very difficult to notice the school if it indeed exists. It's very difficult to say whether it exists or not. I didn't really pay attention. The neighbourhood has developed quite significantly in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And is the road still deep down?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that area, the road is still deep down. The level of the road has not risen in the meantime. The road is still the same. On the right-hand side, you can see the slope. A cartographer can actually read the map and he can tell that there is a -- a sloping ground towards the neighbourhood, and the slant must be several metres. At least that's what I could discern from the photo that I had.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What photo do you talk about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The photo of the neighbourhood where the school in Velagici was. I'm talking about that image that we had on the screen some five or six minutes ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you could see the elevation on that picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know from my previous experience when I passed through that area that the road is on a slant.
