You can actually see it on the image that the road cuts deep into the neighbourhood if you look at the image carefully. Maybe you can display the image again. I can show it to you. It can be proven.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that on both sides of the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that it is the case on both sides, with some differences: The slants are not identical, there is a little bit of a shift towards the right. I can't tell you exactly whether it's a bit to the front or to the back, but in any case, those two parallel sides do show a certain shift in a place there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I leave it to you whether you want to revisit the aerial picture, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think I'd appreciate having the opportunity to think about it over the break, and I see it's about time for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's even beyond that. Witness, we'll take a break. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes. Could you give us an indication, Mr. Traldi, as to where we are in terms of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd estimated two and a half. I think I should be about able to stick to that. I'm told I'm just over two hours at the moment, and so I should finish this session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. There are various opinions about whether you requested two hours or two and a half hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think I may, to some extent, have been responsible for that. I think our initial estimate was two hours and our e-mail last week would have said two and a half, and I'll check and attempt to confirm whether my recollection is accurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That seems to be a good explanation for the difference of --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: My --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- timing. I've seen two and a half hours, colleagues have seen two hours, apparently in different documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: My commanding officer tells me that my recollection is correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I take it that the Defence will not challenge the observations by the commanding officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I was apprised of the two and a half hours. I also saw the two hours but the two and a half hours came later, so I assumed it was two and a half hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, commanding officer is right. We take and break and will resume at 20 minutes past midday.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just to use the time, if we might have P7033 back up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I abuse the time to deal with a matter in relation to Witness GRM251. On the 27th of August, the Chamber denied the Defence motion for protective measures for this witness. On the 11th of December, the Chamber also denied a Defence motion to vary the time-limit to seek certification to appeal the Chamber's original decisions and set a dead-line of the 18th of December for the Defence to file a submission on how to proceed with the proposed evidence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: However, the Defence did not file any submissions on that matter. The Chamber considers the Defence's silence on this matter to mean that the witness will not be recalled; therefore, the Chamber invites the Registry to notify the witness that he is released. Furthermore, considering the limited scope of the witness's substantive testimony, as well the absence of any cross-examination, the Chamber will not rely on the evidence adduced and declares moot the 92 ter motion for this witness. And this concludes the Chamber's decision on the matter. Mr. Traldi, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, you assert in your statement that the Muslim civilian population was treated in accordance with the law. Now, we've just looked at one example of treatment of detained Muslims, the massacre in Velagici. That was an appalling war crime; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, a crime did take place in Velagici but it hadn't been planned. It hadn't been ordered by a superior command. The crime was wilfully committed by individuals. Those individuals were held responsible. They --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- should have been indeed held responsible for what they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- you've gone somewhat beyond my question. You agree with me it was an appalling war crime; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A war crime did take place in Velagici.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I want to ask you about some other examples of treatment of detained Muslims. Now, this is the image you marked earlier. You know that Muslims were detained and beaten in the building you've marked with the school, the Nikola Mackic school, just metres away from the Crisis Staff headquarters; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Members of the Territorial Defence - of the Muslim Territorial Defence - who were in possession of weapons were brought in. They were kept in the school for a short period of time, they were processed there, and from there they were transferred to the Manjaca barracks. There were, indeed, incidents. Individuals came of their own will to do what you said that they did. On several occasions President Banjac intervened --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and prevented those things from taking place.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, in fact, in spite of any reactions by the Crisis Staff members, it happened quite a lot that people were beaten there; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were such incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to ask for a direct answer to my question: Did it happen quite a lot that people were beaten at the Nikola Mackic school?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether that happened often because I was not there all the time. I was not in the municipality building 24/7.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, can we have 65 ter 31814, page 160.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This will be part of your sworn testimony in the Brdjanin case. Now beginning at line 12, you're asked about the Mackic school, and at line 15 you were asked: "And you were fully aware, weren't you, that people were being beaten and beaten to death in that building?" At first you said: "I could not know that in this form. But whenever we noticed that something was happening which was not in accordance with normal human behaviour, we intervened, both with the police and with the military command." And you were asked: "What do you call something that isn't in accord with 'normal human behaviour'?" And at the bottom of this page --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could scroll down.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You responded: "If someone set out to beat someone, then of course we would respond and say that such things must not happen, although in spite of our reactions, such things did happen quite a lot." Do you stand by your Brdjanin testimony that it happened a lot, that people were beaten at the Mackic school?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stand by that statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now separately, the Chamber has received evidence that Muslims were detained at the Kljuc police station, which we also saw is nearby the Crisis Staff headquarters, and received evidence from a Defence witness named Nikola Vracar who stood guard outside the SJB that he could hear people inside being beaten. Now, you were also aware that prisoners were being abused there, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were individual cases, yes. But those happenings were often prevented as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, what happened with the prisoners held at the SJB was the police would interrogate them and then send them to the military prisoner at Manjaca; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After they were processed, those who were members of the Territorial Defence in possession of weapons and for whom it was proven that they were members of the Territorial Defence were transferred to the Manjaca barracks. I don't know if it was a military prison or something else. I was never there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Okay. Sir --

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those who were not in possession of any weapon --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to stop you again.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let's go to page 159 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And here you were asked at the bottom of the page: "But they weren't only being held at Manjaca, were they, prisoners? For a time, at least, they were being held at the police station in Kljuc. You knew that, didn't you?" And you responded: "Mostly they passed through the police station. There, the police carried out certain interrogation, identification. And then sent these people on to Manjaca, to the military prison camp. And this was done by the police in agreement with the military command." Do you stand by the portions of your sworn testimony in the Brdjanin case that I have just read out to you?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's indeed the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, moving away from prisoners, you were aware that on the 1st of June 1992 a village called Prhovo was attacked; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learnt about that in the afternoon hours in the office of the president of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, Prhovo was a Muslim village; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are two villages by the name of Prhovo next to each other. One of them is a Muslim village and the other is a Serb village.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Which one was attacked?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Muslim Prhovo village was searched, and those who were in possession of weapons were brought in because that was the purpose of the search, to find the hidden weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'd put to you that you're not being fully forthcoming at the moment. In fact, you're aware, as you sit there, that women and children were killed during the attack on Prhovo; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I stated once what had happened in Prhovo. You'll find it in one of my statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, Witness, let me be very clear to you. You were asked about an attack on Prhovo. Your answer focused on a search for weapons, which was not the gist of the question. You should tell us here everything you know and not refer to any earlier statement. So the answer was, I take it, but I'm still not certain whether you confirm or not that women and children were killed during the attack on Prhovo. Were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A certain number of women and children were killed in Prhovo, indeed. I thought it would suffice for me to say that I explained that in a statement of mine. I can do it again, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, carefully listen to any question Mr. Traldi is putting to you and answer them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, sir, just so you're clear on the process: Of your previous statements and testimonies, only the specific statement that Mr. Ivetic tendered into evidence is before the Court and part of the record in this case, and so that's why I'm asking you about some other things that we both know you know and you've testified about in the past. So Prhovo was attacked and a number of women, children, and elderly people were killed and they were killed by the VRS military police; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Prhovo was not attacked. There was a search of Prhovo. During the search an incident happened and some women and children were killed during that incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question was whether women, children, and elderly were killed by the VRS military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I beg to differ, Your Honour. The question says: "So Prhovo was attacked ..." At the very beginning. So he is quite accurately responding to the question Mr. Prosecutor posed to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I would object to the fact that he has been trying to do this now several times --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- and no one wants to hear the whole story.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, I think that earlier when there was a question about an attack that the witness did not deny that there was an attack. But let's leave it to that. Let's leave it to that. The question now is whether elderly, women, and children were killed by the VRS military police during this action. I'll refrain from calling it an "attack" or a "search" in Prhovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I would point to the prior transcript where, again, when it was referenced as an attack, he said there was a search. And then it was intervened and said he -- his answer was interrupted. So he has been trying to explain this to Your Honours for ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were elderly -- were elderly, children, and women killed by the VRS military police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were killed during the search.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: By the VRS military police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now please explain what caused them to be killed at that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is how I learned about what happened. In the municipality building in the office of the president of the municipality, I was there with the president, with Colonel Galic, and a few other persons in the afternoon. At one moment, an officer entered the office. I didn't know him. I think that he held the rank of captain. I saw him then and never again. He was in tears. He addressed Colonel Galic and he said, "Colonel, sir, in Prhovo I lost a military policeman, he was killed, and after that I lost command over the platoon of the military police," and what we have already said was done. That is how I heard about it. That is how I learned about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And any further explanation as why elderly, women, and children were killed, rather than someone who may have attacked a military policeman and have killed him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The mentioned captain said that he had lost command; that is to say, that he could not command because people no longer obeyed him, the people whose colleague that military policeman got killed there. So they did what they did on their own. Colonel Galic was very surprised and he left the office together with the captain, and I don't know what happened then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're not aware of any action taken by Colonel Galic at that time to give a follow-up on what was reported to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I have no information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you're not aware, are you, of any VRS military policeman being punished during the war for that massacre?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I never really dealt with that matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: There was also a massacre of unarmed people at the Biljani school in Kljuc in July 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was absent. I wasn't in Kljuc then. It was only a few days later. When I came to Kljuc, I found out that something had happened in Biljani. But, indeed, I never got any concrete information that would indicate what happened, how it happened, and why it happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now what you heard happened was that detained Muslims, more than a hundred of them, were massacred; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not nearly 800. I really don't know about the number. I don't know about the concrete matter. But when I returned from that trip, at one moment I found out that this incident had occurred where a certain number of persons were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Those persons were detained at the time; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, your question was more than a hundred of them were killed, and the witness answers: "No, not nearly 800."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I had initially intended to follow up on that, but when he said: "I really don't know about the number," I thought perhaps I would leave it lie, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but does the number of a hundred people being killed, is that -- Can you say anything about that not having have happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were deaths but how many people died, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you don't know of anybody being punished for this incident either, do you?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the bodies of this incident too were exhumed only after the war from a pit in the Laniste area; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I don't have that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'll turn now to a slightly different topic. We saw on the aerial image that you had reviewed a mosque that had been built after the war, and there was one mosque in Kljuc town at the beginning of the war. It was destroyed in July 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was destroyed. And I don't know what the month was. I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, in fact, none of the mosques in Kljuc municipality survived the war, did they?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I assume that that is the case. But I know for sure that the one in Kljuc was destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, sir, I've reviewed your statement carefully, and I believe paragraph 20 where you refer to "isolated incidents of plunder and the like committed during conflicts between Serb and Muslim forces in Kljuc" is the only place in your evidence where you refer to any crimes committed by Bosnian Serb forces at all. Do you agree with me that there were, in fact, far more than isolated incidents of plunder. There were repeated massacres, abuse of non-Serb prisoners, and destruction of Muslim cultural heritage?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for individual incidents in terms of killings, yes, that did happen, and that was the result of people who were not under any kind of control but simply wanted to plunder and, in that way, if they killed someone, if they destroyed some property, then they would try to conceal that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, sir, the incidents we've talked about, you say people tried to conceal it. You knew, Colonel Galic knew, and nobody was punished. That's the truth, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. No, that's not true. Why would I have to know? It's only later that I found out about something.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And we've seen you were aware of several of these large massacres. You were a member of the Republika Srpska Assembly and the Assembly of the Autonomous Region of the Krajina. Did you keep this information to yourself or did you share it with the members of the Republika Srpska leadership that you regularly interacted with at those assemblies?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the assembly was not informed, I mean, about -- I mean, what happened at individual, local communities.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You never said, "Hey, we've got a problem in Kljuc. We've got people running around massacring dozens, hundreds, taking them together, of unarmed Muslims"?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: All right. I'm going to move on to the last topic that I'm going to address, which I'll do pretty briefly. Sir, you say in your statement people in Kljuc were free to leave if they wanted to. The people leaving had to sign statements saying they wouldn't come back; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know that such statements were signed, but I know that due to instability and due to the lack of security that prevailed in the area, many people expressed the wish to leave, and it was made possible for the civilian protection to organise things to record the names of all the persons who were leaving and organise vehicles, cars, buses, whatever was possible at that moment, so that people could be transferred to the areas that they believed were safe.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You say they wished to leave because of the lack of security. The reason they felt they lacked security, the reason they were afraid was this repeated pattern of crimes committed against the Muslims of Kljuc municipality; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reason for leaving was primarily the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Kljuc was full of refugees, people from other towns in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and I must say that the Muslims of Kljuc were the last people who left their hometown if you take all of Bosnia-Herzegovina into account. People had arrived from many different towns.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We did not catch all of them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because there was a war going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, sir, I'm just going to test two parts of your evidence briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you do so, Mr. Traldi, could you have a look at page 62, the first three lines. In your first sentence of the question, you referred to what the witness said in the statement. In the second sentence, it's a bit unclear whether you put to the witness that what is in his statement is not accurate, or whether you're still referring to his statement assuming that that's what he said. Because if I look at page 28 of the statement, it seems to be pretty clear what the position of this witness is. That's caused me some confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: What I was putting to the witness, and I'll do it very clearly, if you like, Mr. President. What I was putting to the witness was:

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, in your statement, when you say there was some isolated incidents of plunder and the like during these activities, you are dramatically understating the crimes committed against the Muslims; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we have a different page 62, I take it, Mr. Traldi. It was the -- let me just have a look.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'd thought you meant 36, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I don't have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, you have -- don't have the --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It's in reference to paragraph 28 of the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's about the -- what -- I'll just check, one second. Yes. Let me just have a look Mr. -- oh, yes, it's -- let me see, on my left screen I have a different number compared to the ... I referred to -- let me just have a --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It may be 37, lines 9 through 11.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is -- yes. That's exactly what I refer to.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: All right. Then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You understand my confusion. You start by referring to the statement, but apparently it was not entirely clear whether the second sentence is also a reference to his statement or whether it is something you put to him which is not in his statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The second sentence was something I was putting to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Then --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It -- and I'd -- I'll go step by step here. Can we have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 03045.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you say the number again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, sir, this is a decision by the Kljuc Crisis Staff issued the 4th of June, just a couple of days after the massacres at Velagici and Prhovo. And in the first point, it says: "All citizens of the Municipality of Kljuc who express the wish to permanently move out of the Municipality of Kljuc will be enabled to move away from the Municipality of Kljuc in an organised manner." So, first, it was the Crisis Staff's position that the people leaving would be helped to leave if they were leaving permanently; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Permanently. This word that was used, "permanently." The intention was to have the population stay in the municipality of Kljuc, not move out anywhere. That did help in a way. About 1.000 inhabitants of Muslim ethnicity never left Kljuc. They stayed in Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So the rule was those leaving had to leave permanently; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When using the word "permanently," what was intended was not to have people leave. The intention was to have them stay in Kljuc. So it's the other way around.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sir, you're not being asked to interpret the word "permanently," but the question is: Those who did leave had to leave permanently; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So this document is incorrect, according to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is what is written there in order to ensure what I have explained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We're not asking you to ensure anything. We're just asking you whether -- is the document incorrect, according to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document was written exactly -- I mean, it's not incorrect. But the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- intention was to achieve what I've explained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You've answered my question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 03045 receives number P7034, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As to intentions, the Chamber has received evidence that just a few days later Kljuc was represented at a regional meeting where several municipalities decided that the population of Muslims and Croats in their municipalities should be reduced to a level where Serbian control could be ensured.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That's P3753.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now it was, in fact, the intention of the Kljuc authorities to reduce the population of Muslims and Croats in their municipality; wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if he's going to cite a document, he needs to show it to the witness. I'm going to object on that basis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if it's -- it's not necessarily to be done, but if there is any dispute about what the document says then, of course, you could insist on -- you can insist on a literal quote. But if it summarizes it accurately, then of course it's not always needed to put it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I was simply trying to be efficient, Your Honours, but I am happy to call it up if Mr. Ivetic is requesting it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Definitely. If he's going to be comparing and saying is what's in this document the intention of the Kljuc authorities, I think he needs to call it up and he needs to have the exact language in front of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it's clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I can't remember off the top of my head what the document says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you say due to the -- I wouldn't know either, but if you say that's a reason why I would like to have a look at it, then of course you're fully entitled to look at it. And Mr. Traldi has called it up already. Mr. Traldi?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: But we don't see it yet on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And this is the conclusions adopted at a subregional meeting of political representatives of several municipalities. We see Kljuc is the last one. And I'm afraid I don't recall what point number it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: But I think we need to turn to the second page in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, point 6. "All seven municipalities in our sub-region agree that Muslims and Croats should move out of our municipalities until a level is reached where a Serbian authority can be maintained and implemented on its own territory in each of these municipalities." Now that, in fact, was the position of the Kljuc authorities; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I don't know about this document. This is the first time I see it and I've never heard of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: All right. As to the population, you said a moment ago a thousand stayed. There were 17.500 Muslims at the beginning of the war; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And last point on this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have P4105 just for a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could you repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, sir, this is a set of declarations of people leaving Kljuc municipality. If you look under the word "declaration," second paragraph, you see this person declares: "My family and I are leaving Kljuc Municipality voluntarily and permanently," and that they've signed it. And so does this refresh your recollection as to whether people leaving Kljuc had to sign statements saying they were leaving for good?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stand by the statement I've already provided, and this statement shows that, nevertheless, it was through the civilian protection that this work was done.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Okay. Then I'm done with that topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And very briefly, can we have 31883.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, sir, I'm going to go back to the issue of the Velagici school and whether it's still there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would have one additional question in relation to the previous matter. Witness, in paragraph 28 of your statement, we see that you said: "When leaving the municipality of Kljuc, all citizens were allowed to sell their property or gift it to others or leave it to their fellow residents to look after, but it is also probable that there were some isolated instances of blackmail by individuals. I do not know of and never saw anyone sign a document about leaving for good or relinquishing their property to the Kljuc municipality." When we looked at, this statement, seems to be a form where just the data of the individuals are filled in, which also suggests that it was not incidental, and it was not blackmail by individuals but it was rather systemic, it being stemmed by the officials of Kljuc, the commission for gathering information on the departure of the population. Do you have an explanation as why you say it was individuals, it was not systemic, whereas everything in this document suggests that it was not by individuals and it was systemic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I meant in my statement was, I mean, when I said that often some individuals did that, were forced to do that, I meant that there were certain people who would force some citizens of Muslim ethnicity to leave their apartment to them and to sign that they had given it as a present or something like that. So I'm referring to individuals, not what the civilian protection did. The civilian protection did their work as defined by the decision. However, this statement clearly shows that it is not that the apartment is being returned to the municipality but to the owner, and in this situation it is Sip Kljuc that is the owner. So the apartment is not being given to the municipality but to the owner of the apartment; although, in the former Yugoslavia, we had a specific situation, a special situation as far as housing was concerned. So the owner of this apartment was Sip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I didn't touch upon specifically on the ownership of the department which is mentioned in this document. But leaving voluntarily and permanently is part of the form. And, of course, what we would like to know is that where the document we earlier looked at, that was the statement which talks not about, please, Muslims and Croats, stay, but is talking about permanently leaving, if we look at the document you say you have no knowledge about what was discussed, that the number of non-Serbs should be reduced so that the Serbs could exercise control, and in view of the apparently 16.500 -- or was it -- yes, who were initially there of which 15.500 then -- or did I mix up the number?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. 17-. So, well, the more than 50.000 who'd left, that all these documents are suggesting a situation which is quite different from what you are telling us in your evidence, and I wonder whether you have an explanation for this, what suggests is an inconsistency between your testimony and what we read in those documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I rise to correct Your Honour that the question posed by Your Honour included the evidence from the statement which did talk about relinquishing property. It said, the second transcript, which is with the smaller page numbers, page 44, your question begins at line 15, and at line 22 through 23 is about leaving for good or relinquishing property. And so I believe that Your Honour's question was being answered by the witness, and, indeed, he did mention relinquishing property and that has to be taken into account when considering this document, which does not talk about relinquishing property but returning property to the owner of the property as the witness has testified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Again, that is page 44?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It's 44.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It should be I think 70 -- 70 or 69, I think, it would be on the big transcript. On the little transcript that we have on our private monitors, it's 44 and specifically lines 22 through 23.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When I was using the word "relinquishing property," I was quoting the witness, and the blackmail by individuals does not specifically refer to either relinquishing property or moving out. Let me just see.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The sentence says: "When leaving the Municipality of Kljuc, all citizens were allowed to sell their property or gift it to others or leave it to their fellow residents to look after, but it is also probable that there were some isolated instances of blackmail by individuals." So I put it to you that blackmail by individuals can only relate to property based upon the statement, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, then, I think my question was then broader. The question was also about permanently leaving. And I did not specifically focus, as I said, on this document for this witness. But you said there were a few opportunities either to sell or to -- let me read it again. They were allowed to sell or gift it to others or leave it to their fellow residents to look after. Couldn't they just leave it as it was and then return? Without asking anyone else to look after it at that moment and not selling it and not give it as a present? Just leave and return.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's how things were at the time. I can't say now whether things could have been done differently. But what I told you is my opinion, which is corroborated by the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I have another question. What had to be done with the real estate was part of the systemic approach because it appears as one of the preprinted parts of this form. Would you agree with me that that suggests or that -- could you even confirm that any declaration on departure was supposed to have a paragraph on what to do with the real estate rather than just leave it as it was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am not a legal expert. I wouldn't be able to define the appearance of the form, to improve it on what it was, actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 31883.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As it comes up, sir, you're -- we were just discussing what was done with property. You've said a couple of times people had the right to sell it. In fact, you're aware, aren't you, that the Kljuc War Presidency passed a decision saying people who were leaving couldn't sell their property?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that decision. However, things -- things were done in practice as I described them in the statement and as we have discussed so far.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Okay. We're looking at an aerial now. This is the area around where the Velagici school used to be; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm trying to recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, if you look at what looks like the white outlines of something very much like a number 8 roughly in the centre, that's in fact the cemetery for the people who were killed at Velagici; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm afraid, Mr. Traldi, I can't recognise what looks like a number 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It's -- perhaps that was overly evocative of me but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What are you pointing at? It's nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether it's an 8 or not is -- may also depend on how we learned to write an 8 at school.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Perhaps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It's more rectangular than an 8 would typically be, certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we zoom in on it so that it's clear for the witness. He's not being asked to mark anything at this moment. Could we zoom in to the centre of the -- yes, even more. Even more. A little bit further. Now we have to move up slightly. Yes. Perhaps this assists, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It does, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now that -- what we see in the centre of the image, a rectangle that perhaps does not, in fact, look like a number 8, that's the cemetery for the people killed at Velagici village; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you recognise it as the cemetery, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't recognise the cemetery. But since I passed that way, I can say that the cemetery indeed is somewhere around there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In view of that answer, I think -- first, I'd put to you it's our position that that's the cemetery; and, second, I'd suggest to you that for someone driving by that area, it would, in fact, be pretty easy to tell that there is not a school there; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no school there. There was never a school where the cemetery is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Which -- you described earlier that the school was to the side of where the cemetery is now. Can you describe for the Judges --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Opposite. Opposite.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: On the opposite side.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can you describe for the Judges and for me where on this image the school used to be?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps we could have the assistance of the usher if he moves the cursor in such a way upon the instructions of the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Actually, Your Honour, it might be simplest to have him mark, I think, Your Honour, if that's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but first to see whether you are -- whether he recognises the same feature. Could we move the cursor a little bit further to the right. A little bit further to the right, to the right, to the right, stop. A little bit further down. Witness, were you aware that where the cursor is now that that is the rectangular feature which Mr. Traldi referred to earlier in his questions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. This rectangular form represents the location of the cemetery. But if we now want to locate the school, then we have to move the cursor across the main road towards the desk; that is, towards my desk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Move the cursor towards me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's move it a little bit down, and you say step if we reach the level where you think the school was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Across the road, across the road. Very well. And now move to the right. And here, this is where the school was. In this area here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now we could ask the witness to mark it, but at least we now know that he's talking about the same feature as you were talking about. Could you, Witness, first -- and I leave it to you, Mr. Traldi, how to mark it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, if you could just draw an X where you believe the school to have been.

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And now perhaps we could ask the witness to put a circle around where the cemetery is so that -- no, this is the marking of a previous image which is not what is supposed to be on the ... okay. Could we either have the marking again or ask the witness to again mark with a cross the location of the school.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And, Witness, could you please put a circle around where you identified the cemetery to be.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd tender the image and that completes my cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Image marked by the witness, Madam Registrar, would receive number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Number P7035, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. And one final question from me, Witness. Could I ask you again: Are you certain that from the road you couldn't see either it's the cemetery or the school because the road was so deeply -- that you couldn't see it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I never said that. I said that from the road you could see the cemetery but that you could not see the school from the road because the road was at such an angle and at such a level that you simply couldn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Any questions in re-examination, Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I also think we're at the time for a break, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. What -- how much time do you think you would need?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm looking at about 30, 35 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's try to see whether we can conclude the evidence of the witness today. And, Mr. Traldi, I know that you are -- you may need some time as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can we excuse the next witness, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the next witness can be excused. Mr. Kalabic, we'll take a break. We would like to see you back in 20 minutes. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll resume at quarter to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps I use the opportunity to briefly address a matter which is about the remaining issue from the testimony of Novica Andric. 30th of September, during the testimony of that witness, the Defence made reference to an interview with a witness where the witness testified that the polygraph test was administered; transcript pages 26416 to -417. The Chamber proceeded to request submissions from the parties concerning the probative value of this polygraph test and asked the parties to clarify how much time would be required to prepare submissions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Prosecution informed the Chamber that a week would be sufficient. However, the Defence requested further time; transcript pages 26427 to -430. The Chamber contacted the Defence via e-mail on the 27th of October, and again on the 2nd of December, requesting a time-line for submissions, but as of today's date the Defence has not responded, and both parties are hereby invited to make submissions by the 21st of January. Mr. Ivetic, if you're ready to re-examine the witness, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. If we can have -- oops, my screen is dark. I hope we have e-court. Can we have P3771 to start off with.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can stay at page 1 in the English but turn to the middle of page 2 in the Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: This is a meeting, the 23rd of December, of the SDS Municipal Board of Executive Committee in Kljuc. You were asked about Mr. Koljevic's statements about a tri-part Bosnia previously, and I would like to look at what Mr. Vinko Kondic says at the bottom of the page in English and in the middle of the second page in Serbian: "We have to implement the federal and not Bosnian laws because" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic is supposed not to speak at such a volume that we can hear it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'll start again.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: "We have to implement the federal and not Bosnian laws because the Bosnian laws are past by outvoting the Serbs." And then we have Mr. Veljko Kondic who says -- or he says: "Veljko Kondic will be responsible for co-operation with the SDA." Now, does this accurately report the position, at least, of the Kljuc SDS that co-operation with the SDA was required and that any laws which outvoted one of the three constituent peoples would not be considered valid? It's --

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is that a question for me?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Veljko Kondic was supposed to continue co-operation with the SDA on the issue of the order of things that Vinko Kondic proposed although, even before that, we talked and co-operated with the SDA. I emphasized that this was just an attempt to reinforce co-operation with the SDA with regard to certain topics.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [In English] And here we've been talking about Serbs and the SDA, but there's no mention of the Croats, the third constituent peoples of the BiH. What was the population statistics of ethnic Croats in Kljuc?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was slightly less than 1 per cent of Croats in Kljuc. I don't know exactly how many there were, but less than 1 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And in relation to the constitution of Bosnia-Herzegovina from its time in the SFRY, could that constitution be changed or could that republic secede from the former Yugoslavia without the vote of all three constituent peoples?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The constitution of the Socialist Federal Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina has an article that I'm going to paraphrase. That article defines that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Witness, and then we'll hear Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The constitution of the Socialist Federal Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina has an article that I'm going to paraphrase. That article defines that two peoples cannot over-vote a third people, regardless of what that people was. However, that article of the constitution was not honoured, and there was over-voting of the Serb deputies in the Assembly of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think the connection between this last question and my cross is a bit attenuated at best.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi represented the quotation of Mr. Koljevic as a tripartite Bosnia as meaning something different than what is under the constitution. I think I'm entitled to go back to the legal framework of what tripartite Bosnia-Herzegovina means, not what the Prosecution wants it to mean.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, if you would finish what you wanted to tell us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I maintain my submission that the connection is attenuated. Given Mr. Ivetic's response, I think he's focussing on a different part of Mr. Koljevic's remarks than the part to which I sought to call the witness's attention to and that underscores, I think, my original point which is that this is questionably arising from cross-examination at best.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, he used this document in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- Mr. -- yes, the use of a document is not the same as putting a specific question. Mr. Ivetic, could you please keep in mind that the link between what was raised in cross-examination and what you raise in re-examination. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Today at temporary transcript page 15 and onwards, Mr. Traldi asked you about Kljuc's joining of the ARK. I would like to ask you about the Kljuc Assembly declaration that Mr. Traldi had --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Which is P7030, if we can call that up.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall how the voting went on this decision in the Kljuc Municipal Assembly to join the ARK? Did Muslim delegates or assemblymen participate in this vote?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not about the ARK joining anything. It's just about the accepting of the name, and the municipality of Banja Luka became part of the autonomous region. Muslim deputies were against that decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now if we take one step backward, the voting for the decision to join the ARK in the first place, did Muslim deputies take part in that vote?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object to that description. I think Mr. Ivetic is conflating the ARK and the community of municipalities in his question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, it may be clear from paragraph 1 of this document that there were several decisions on joining --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The community of -- yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Co-operation of municipalities. I leave it exactly at that neutral expression. Could you be very, very precise because apparently there was one decision which was confirmed and there was a decision adopted, a decision, I take it, the one adopted that would enter into force on the day of its adoption; that is, on the 16th of January.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please clearly distinguish between whatever decisions you would like to refer to.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, in relation to the decision, the earlier adopted decision that is referenced in paragraph 1 of this decision, to join Kljuc municipality to the regional community of Bosnia -- pardon me, to the Banja Luka Community of Municipalities, did Muslim delegates or deputies participate in that vote?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the decision was passed on Kljuc joining the regional community of Banja Luka, a hundred per cent of the voters in Banja Luka were in favour. The deputies were then elected to represent Kljuc in the Association of Communities. One of the deputies was Omer Filipovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And did Omer Filipovic attend meetings or sessions of the Assembly of the Autonomous Region of Krajina?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to what I know, he attended such meetings once or twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think again, Your Honours, we've created confusion. And I'd just ask Mr. Ivetic to clarify if with his last question he meant the ZOBK or the ARK.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I meant the ARK. And if it helps, Mr. Traldi, your document from cross-examination number 31815, page 16, that's the source of my question where it says ARK, and that's the testimony of this witness in another proceeding.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Just so we can be clear, is this the same Omer Filipovic we talked about that was a Bosnian Muslim and that later led the attacks of 27 May 1992?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, one and the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now at transcript -- temporary transcript page 20, Mr. Traldi said that by April 1992 the Serbs controlled the important positions in Kljuc and the power in Kljuc was in Serb hands. Sir, the question I want to ask you: Did Serbs hold important positions in Kljuc even prior April of 1992 essentially ever since the 1990 multiparty elections?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I understood your question well, we are talking about important positions in employment. Is that what your question is about?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In the government. In the local government in Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the local government of Kljuc, yes. As I have already told you, Serbs distributed -- or, rather, split the power with Muslims 50/50. I'm talking about the most important positions which were subject of distribution.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And were the Muslims who were put in important positions replaced; that is to say, were Serbs named to those positions or were Serbs -- or were the Muslims still there formally in those positions?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're referring to Kljuc municipality, Muslims did come to work up to the 27th of May, 1992. And then on that day, those people who occupied various positions in the municipality did not turn up for work, and then from then on, they stopped coming all together.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And who --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic could --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you are still on this subject, I will wait for a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I was going to ask about the Kljuc Assembly. If you want to ask about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it's about one of the previous questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Then go ahead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, you answered one question by saying: "When the decision was passed on Kljuc joining the Regional Community of Banja Luka, a hundred per cent of the voters in Banja Luka were in favour." I'm a bit puzzled by "hundred per cent of the voters in Banja Luka." Was it a decision taken by voters in Banja Luka or was it a decision which was passed by the Kljuc authorities? Could you help me out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. If I mentioned Banja Luka, I must be tired. A hundred per cent of the deputies of the Municipal Assembly of Kljuc were in favour of that, and the voting took place in Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That clarifies the matter. Then if you would say a hundred per cent, that included the Muslim --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, following the 1990 elections the Kljuc Municipal Assembly, who had a majority of the seats therein?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the elections, the SDS got over 50 per cent of the seats. Whereas the SDA and the IMBO, the two Muslim parties that worked together, got 20 per cent of the seats in the assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to look at P2867, page 3 in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: While we wait for it, I could say that this is the document that we looked at earlier dated 14 May 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: May we have the number again.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: P2867. Page 3 in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: This is the meeting 14th May that you were present for with Colonel Galic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we can have page 3 in the English. And if we could focus on what President Banjac has to say. It's, I believe, near the end of the page in the B/C/S and it is the approximately fourth complete paragraph from the bottom in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: "The president of Kljuc SO, Jovo Banjac, said that in Kljuc the policy of finding a peaceful solution to the problems was still being pursued. He also said that Kljuc municipality will work for the army with all its available strength. He proposed to set up a military police department to control the behaviour of reservists on leave." Now, it was suggested to you by Mr. Traldi that this meeting followed the meeting in Sarajevo and that in -- a meeting the same day you --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: No, sorry. Not -- I'd -- I'd object to the characterisation of what I suggested. It was not suggested this followed a meeting in Sarajevo. It was suggested this followed a meeting in Banja Luka --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Banja Luka --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- two days earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- two days earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- at the Serb assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Where it was, you suggested, that you -- that you took the objectives from these prior meetings and sent them down to Kljuc. Does this accurately reflect the objectives as understood by the president of the Municipal Assembly of Kljuc and of the Crisis Staff of Kljuc of what the intent and goal of all the efforts of the parties, at least on the Serb side were, at this time?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that this is about strategic goals, or strategic objectives, that we were informed about at that meeting. The president portrayed the Serbian leadership of Kljuc municipality, and what the president said can be corroborated by a statement by Asim Ekrecic [phoen] who was the president of the Executive Board who said in one of his statements that the leadership of the SDS in Kljuc was democratic, tolerant, and that it was not difficult to co-operate with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. If we could also look at 65 ter number 02992.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: To refresh your recollection, this is the report from Radio Kljuc, Hronika, about a memorial event in September of 1991 which you attended regarding the --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, this strikes me as also beyond the scope of cross. I didn't ask about this event, I didn't ask about the memorial, and it's chronologically before basically any event that I asked about.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Is it before -- is it around the time-period of Mr. Koljevic's comments? Was Mr. Buha and Mr. Koljevic in the same branch of government? Do you know what I'm asking the witness, Counsel? I haven't even yet had my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I suppose it's two and a half months before -- or three months before Mr. Koljevic's remarks.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So if we could turn to page 3 in both versions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's usually the -- there is no formal objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sorry, I will use the word I -- "I object."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This document is beyond the scope of cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, because otherwise, Mr. Ivetic, we could not rule on it, but we'd have to rule on it --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yeah, agreed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But Mr. Ivetic was already satisfied that he was on the right. Mr. Ivetic, you may put that question to the witness, but I also urge you not to dwell too far away from what was dealt with in cross. And I would also like you to keep an eye on the clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm trying, Your Honours. I'm hoping to conclude very shortly. I should be able to in about three, four minutes. If we can look at -- I'm told it should be on page 3. This is not -- on the B/C/S, it should also be page 3. Yes. And it's -- now we have both on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And here we have the comments where it says that Dr. Karadzic and Dr. Koljevic and Mr. Crncevic had been announced but did not come to the meeting but they were represented by Professor Aleksa Buha. And he talks here about the task of the SDS, he said, was to make the Serbian people aware, and this implied a revival of the national identity. "We have to reach back to our national tradition, said Professor Buha, which has been longer and more important than was thought. We should go back to Saint Sava and our roots, he said, to find answers important for the Serbian national identity. Another task for the SDS was to get the Serbian people to clear things with their brothers with whom they had been living in these parts for centuries, the Muslims and Croats. If all the three peoples had satisfied themselves that the new nation would come to nothing and that the regime so far had been a regime of pressure, what remained was for each to go back to their own tradition and come together at a latter point to clarify matters in terms of finding a joint answer as to how," and then we have to go to the next page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: "How we were to live, if not together as one, then side by side. In this context each group should organise the things for themselves in the way that would suit them best." First question I would like to ask you, sir, is here Mr. Buha is talking about a new nation that didn't work. Now Mr. Traldi asked you about a nation that would disappear from Mr. Koljevic's comments. The question I have for you is in relation to the south Slavs, when they formed Yugoslavia after the world wars, was there a new Yugoslavia nationality that was enacted? That's the first question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, in the former state of Yugoslavia, there was a possibility, as far as I can remember, for those who wanted to declare themselves as Yugoslavs to do so. Whether they were treated as a separate nation or a separate people or not, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And the second question is: During -- after the multiparty elections in the 1990s, and especially in Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1990, 1991, 1992, did people start changing their nationality registers to move away from the Yugoslav nationality that we have discussed?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A very hard question for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. Then I'll move on. In relation to separating, the -- your statement, I believe in paragraph 4, talks about the Muslims creating the Donji Kraji Kljuc municipality in 1991, and the question I have is: Did the Serb members of local government continue to co-operate with the same Bosnian Muslim leaders that had set up this separate municipality in 1991 even after they had done so?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, co-operation continued. The Muslim representatives who were elected to the municipality, they came to their jobs regularly, they carried out their duties, discussions were held, certain joint solutions were found. Sometimes it wasn't that easy or quick to reach agreement, but we did live together until the 27th of May when the convoy of the army was attacked.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And my last question is in relation to the school, the Nikola Mackic school that Mr. Traldi asked you about.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would like to turn to the transcript that was shown. I think it's 65 ter number 31814. And I think we want page 161 of that, which should be approximately one page after the section that was used with you by Mr. Traldi. And it should correlate to transcript page 22676 of the underlying Brdjanin transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I'd like to focus on lines 10 through 15 with you. The question that was posed goes as follows: "Q. And the point that I'm trying to make, Mr. Kalabic, is that you, the Crisis Staff, could have simply told the police they could not use this building as a prison? "A. This did not last for a long time, and I think that the Crisis Staff contributed to the fact that people were not longer interrogated in the school." First question I have for you, sir: Do you stand by your answer as recorded in the Brdjanin transcript as being truthful and accurate?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And the school in issue, is that -- which school is it, just so we're clear?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nikola Mackic in Kljuc. I marked him on the video-clip [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I thank you for your patience. I know we went longer. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I thank Your Honours for the extra time, and everyone else in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, everyone else in the courtroom which allows us to conclude the testimony of this witness. Mr. Traldi, unless you are going to spoil the effort.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I wouldn't want to spoil the effort. I might ask three questions, if we have a minute for it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Three short questions. I'm looking at the booth and I do not hear of a clear opposition. So, therefore, with much appreciation for the flexibility and the co-operation, you can put three questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the witness is invited to answer those questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 07095. Further Cross-examination by Mr. Traldi:

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And while this comes up, sir, Mr. Ivetic asked you a moment ago if Omer Filipovic was one of Kljuc's representatives in the ZOBK and suggested to you that he had attended sessions of the ARK Assembly. Now, first, you're aware that in late May 1992 Mr. Filipovic surrendered to the VRS, was taken to Manjaca, and was eventually killed there; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Second --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we can turn to -- I believe it's page 2 in both languages. And, I'm sorry, we need page 3 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: This is a list of representatives in the ARK Assembly. If we look at numbers 89 through 93, we see the Kljuc representatives, including yourself. Those people are all Serbs; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO KALABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a confusion here. The ZOBK, Omer Filipovic and a few other Muslims were deputies there. And when the name was changed from ZOBK to ARK, then the Muslims abandoned that association and they were no longer deputies in Krajina. Let's be clear, there are two terms: The Community of Municipalities of Banja Luka, they were members there; when the name was changed, they were no longer deputies. They abandoned their posts.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender this document and that will be all the questions I have for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 7095 receives number P7036, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. Just to clarify matters. Earlier we had this discussion about the assembly meetings. Mr. Traldi sought clarification from Mr. Ivetic whether Mr. Filipovic attended such meetings once or twice, referring to the ARK, to the ARK. Do I understand, Witness, that Mr. Filipovic never attended a assembly meeting of the ARK?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He attended the first session after the name was changed. After that, never again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Was the name changed at that session or was it changed before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before. The name was changed before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: By whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Whoever was authorised to do that, the ARK Assembly. I don't know exactly, but I believe it was the ARK Assembly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's what's puzzling me, as a matter of fact. So you say he attended one meeting after the ARK Assembly had changed the name but not after that any further, or don't you know? Please tell us if you don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am sure that he attended one after the name was changed and never again after that. I am sure that he did attend one session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Kalabic, this concludes your testimony. I would like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague, a long way, and for having answered all the questions that were put to you. I wish you a safe return home again. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn for the day. We will resume tomorrow, Wednesday, the 21st of January, 2015, in this same courtroom, I, at 9.30. And do I understand well that we'll hear the testimony of the next witness in closed session?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
